persona.description: Casual music listener who has never used a DAW
persona.music_goal: A short catchy electronic melody with included instruments, repeating playback, saved project, and export if discoverable

study_method.interface: Native GUI in isolated Xvfb display :141, mouse.py driver only
study_method.read_sources: Required AGENTS.md only; no repository implementation, docs, tests, prior studies, MCP, or app internal state used to choose actions.

goal_outcome.repeat_playback: loop range configured; sustained audition limited by audio disconnects
goal_outcome.export: WAV and MP3 completed with visible success banners
goal_outcome.subjective_audio_judgment: Not made. Participant did not claim to hear or assess catchiness. Coordinator verified nonzero actual capture; exported audio requires separate coordinator verification.

created_music.name: Neon steps
tracks: R1 Mini using Lead Sync Lead preset
created_music.melody: Eight evenly spaced 1/8 notes: C4, Eb4, G4, F4, Eb4, C4, D4, Eb4. Four consecutive copies; fourth raised one octave through Clip > Octave up.

chronological_discoveries.expectation: I expect Play to let me hear the included rhythm and Add track to let me choose a melody instrument.
chronological_discoveries.observed: A project named Midnight circuit is open with one Circuit drums waveform track and a visible Loop button. I do not yet know what MIDI means.

chronological_discoveries.actions: Play; Details; Close; Audio setup; Output menu; choose Rill lab paced output; Apply; Retry playback
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Play should start music; error instructions should reconnect it.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Initial error was visible and offered useful Details and recovery controls. Details instructed checking output. Choosing the one alternate output and Retry caused Pause label, a moving playhead and green meters. No actual audio verified yet.
chronological_discoveries.classification: Environment-confounded playback issue; recovery affordances successful

chronological_discoveries.actions: Add track > Add instrument track > select R1 Mini > Add instrument track > Preset > Lead Sync Lead > close
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Choose an electronic melody instrument and start making notes.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Three built-in choices are easy to scan; R1 Mini is identified as Synth only after selection. Its many oscillator/filter controls are unfamiliar, but named presets offer a usable shortcut. Lead Sync Lead chosen. Closing shows a new R1 Mini track with New pattern already created. Browser says 0 plug-ins despite three built-ins shown; that was briefly confusing.

chronological_discoveries.actions: Double-click pattern; Keyboard; Cancel; double-click lower body; Cancel; right-click; Edit notes
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Double-click the new pattern to put notes in it; Keyboard might open the musical keyboard.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Both double-click attempts opened a rename form. Keyboard opened a typing keyboard, not piano keys. Right-click revealed Edit notes first, which opened the piano grid. A beginner had no visible hint explaining this route.

chronological_discoveries.actions: Pencil; first click; Snap 1/8; Length 1/8; erase initial short note; draw eight notes; Play
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Greenish rows look like safe notes; evenly spaced notes should make a short melody.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Pencil gives clear Draw notes / Drag to set length instruction. Initial note was tiny. Snap and Length menus let me make uniform note blocks; I drew a rising-and-falling eight-note phrase inside the Clip end marker. C4/G4/F4/D4 labels helped orient me. Playhead moves, but sound is not yet verified.
successes: Found Pencil and Erase without help
Made eight evenly spaced notes using 1/8 snap and length

chronological_discoveries.actions: Clip > Loop this clip; Play; Back; dismiss output error; rename pattern Neon steps; File > Save as; full path in session exports
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Loop should repeat the melody and Save as should preserve my work with a new name.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Loop this clip visibly shortened green loop range to one bar (2.1 seconds). Playback failed again within roughly ten seconds. Naming and Save as succeeded, with project title Neon steps and no unsaved dot. File menu also clearly exposes Export WAV. Actual sound still unverified.

chronological_discoveries.actions: Context menu Duplicate; Duplicate tool twice; Select; drag loop-range right edge toward bar 5; Ctrl+S; File > Export WAV; inspect Type; keep WAV; Export; OK
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Repeat the phrase across the drum rhythm and export the whole song.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Duplicate places each copy immediately after the current one. Tool hint Click a clip to duplicate is clear. Four phrases now match the drum length. Dragging loop end a long distance only lengthened range to 2.1.3 (2.4 seconds), not bar 5; uncertain whether application or simulated input. Ctrl+S did not visibly clear dirty dot. Export defaults to whole Arrangement, shows 8.571 seconds, and completed with success banner. Types include MP3 though menu is Export WAV.
chronological_discoveries.audio_evidence: Coordinator reports actual nonzero audio in 12-second capture near 16:38:12; no subjective listening assessment by participant.

chronological_discoveries.actions: Range > Loop playback over arrangement; File > Save; fourth phrase > Edit notes > Clip > Octave up; Back; File > Save; Re-export last WAV (replace)
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Make the whole piece repeat and make the last repetition higher for variation.
chronological_discoveries.observed: Range menu makes whole-arrangement looping easy after drag trouble. Menu Save clears dirty dot. Octave up visibly changes fourth phrase C4/G4/F4/D4 labels to C5/G5/F5/D5. Re-export succeeded quickly without repeating settings.

chronological_discoveries.actions: File > Export WAV > Type MP3 > Export > OK; File > Open > Neon steps.rill; fourth phrase > Edit notes; Back
chronological_discoveries.expectation: Have a familiar shareable file and be able to return to the saved song.
chronological_discoveries.observed: MP3 export success banner shown. Open picker showed Neon steps.rill (3.3 MB). Reopened project retained all four phrases, whole-arrangement loop range, and high final phrase (C5/G5/F5/D5 labels). Final view returned to Arranger.
chronological_discoveries.environment_update: Coordinator established earlier Ctrl+S no-op was missing Xvfb window focus after native picker; not an established RILL defect. Driver later restored clicked-window focus.

issues.title: Double-clicking a new pattern leads to naming, not note creation
steps: Add instrument track with R1 Mini
Cancel and double-click lower pattern body
Right-click pattern and choose Edit notes
issues.expected: Double-clicking the blank musical pattern would open a place to create notes; Keyboard might open piano keys.
issues.observed: Both double-click attempts opened Rename. Keyboard expanded a typing keyboard. Edit notes was only found by right-clicking. This delayed the first note by about 47 seconds.
issues.confidence: high for observed behavior; medium for broader novice prevalence

issues.title: Device browser says 0 plug-ins while showing three built-in instruments
steps: Inspect Device browser header and Built-in collection
issues.expected: The instrument count would match the instruments available to choose.
issues.observed: Top-right says 0 plug-ins while three cards and All plug-ins 3/Built-in 3 are visible. This briefly raised doubt whether instruments were installed.
issues.recovery: Selected R1 Mini and successfully added it.
issues.confidence: high for visible mismatch; medium for novice impact

issues.title: Export WAV label hides that MP3 is also available
issues.expected: A command labeled Export WAV appears to offer WAV output only.
issues.observed: The dialog offers WAV, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, and MP3. MP3 was discovered only after entering the WAV command and inspecting Type.
issues.confidence: high for label/available-types mismatch; medium for impact

issues.title: Loop-range edge drag did not reach intended bar
steps: Create four consecutive one-bar melody clips
Drag green loop-range right edge from x488 to x1066 at y217
issues.expected: Loop range would expand from one bar to all four bars.
issues.observed: After drag the loop ended at 2.1.3 (2.411 seconds), close to the old endpoint instead of bar 5. One attempt only; driver/event timing is a possible explanation.
issues.recovery: Range > Loop playback over arrangement set correct 1.1–5.1 range.
issues.confidence: low as product defect; high as observed failed attempt

issues.title: Playback output repeatedly disconnected in isolated audio environment
issues.severity: major for audition task; not attributed to product
steps: Audio setup > Output > Rill lab paced output > Apply
Later play edited melody and loop it
issues.expected: Playback would remain active long enough to hear and assess repeated music.
issues.observed: Initial Play displayed Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Details showed ALSA snd_pcm_avail_delay I/O error (5). Alternate output briefly showed moving transport/meters, but error returned in later attempts. Coordinator verified nonzero recorded signal near one playback attempt, so some output occurred.
issues.recovery: Temporary recovery through named alternate output and Retry; offline exports succeeded.
issues.confidence: high for error and recurrence; low for RILL responsibility

issues.title: Ctrl+S failed after native picker because desktop focus was missing
issues.expected: Shortcut would save project and clear unsaved dot.
issues.observed: Dirty dot remained after shortcut. File > Save later cleared it; coordinator confirmed Xvfb focus on root after native picker with no window manager and corrected driver focus behavior.
issues.recovery: Used File > Save; reopened project confirmed final contents.
issues.confidence: high for environment attribution from coordinator

successes: Add track > Add instrument track exposed a small, manageable set of included instruments.
Named R1 Mini presets provided a usable route around unfamiliar oscillator/filter controls.
Instrument creation automatically supplied a blank pattern.
Pencil and Erase labels and Draw notes / Drag to set length instructions helped create notes.
Separate Snap and Length menus allowed uniform 1/8-note phrase construction.
Duplicate tool instruction Click a clip to duplicate was immediately understandable.
Clip > Loop this clip and Range > Loop playback over arrangement were effective once found.
Export defaults covered the whole arrangement and displayed duration before export.
Export success banners and re-export last file action gave clear confirmation and efficient revision.
Saved project reopened with all four phrases and the raised final phrase intact.
unresolved_questions: Would a true beginner discover right-click Edit notes without facilitator persistence?
Why did the loop-end drag advance only a small amount in this driver session?
Can playback remain stable outside this isolated audio setup?
What do all oscillator/filter controls and export dither/headroom terminology mean to a novice? Named presets/defaults avoided needing answers.
limitations: Simulated novice, not an empirical human participant; results describe this one interaction path.
Audio output transport was unstable in isolated environment, limiting audition, sound balancing, and perceived catchiness assessment.
Some screenshots captured transient blur or native-dialog black paint; settled screenshots were used for findings.
Ctrl+S no-op was confirmed environment focus issue and is not a RILL defect.
Loop drag observation is one attempt and may be driver/event-timing related.
Started from coordinator-provided Midnight circuit project with existing drum audio rather than an empty project.
